newsitem.title: RUSSIA: D Morgan Grenfell says take profits on Rostelekom.
newsitem.headline: D Morgan Grenfell says take profits on Rostelekom.

text.p: Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said on Thursday that holders of shares in Russian long-distance phone operator Rostelekom should take profits now.

"We like the stock, admire the company's infrastructure expansion, and applaud its relative financial transparency," it said in a research note. "Nevertheless, this looks like a time to take profit and look for greater relative value elsewhere."
It said that Rostelekom's plans to issue a Eurobond and American Depository Receipts (ADRs) this year could push the share price up.
But it said Rostelekom's valuation ceiling is $4.50. Rostelekom fell to $4.23 on the Russian Trading System at 0930 GMT on Thursday from $4.34 at Wednesday's close.

The London investment bank said it had recommended buying Rostelekom last November when fears over a merger with Svyazinvest had sent the share price down to around $2.20. It said Rostelekom had outperformed the market by 27 percent so far this year.

It said International Accounting Standards (IAS) financial data for Rostelekom in 1996 have not been released. But it said its analysis of Russian Accounting Standards data suggests Rostelekom's operating profit in 1996 may have dropped about 3.3 percent from 1995.
"We would therefore recommend taking profits either now or in the run-up to the ADR," it said. The Russian market should offer greater relative value than Rostel at current prices."
